summary: Lists WinRM limitations (no credential delegation for most auth types, blocked Windows Update API calls, failed installs, non-interactive sessions, no DPAPI) and mitigations: CredSSP or Kerberos delegation, become, or scheduled tasks.
questions: Why can't my Windows task access a network share over WinRM?
Why do some programs refuse to install over WinRM?
How do I get around the double-hop problem in Ansible?
Why does SQL Server install fail through Ansible?
Does become remove all WinRM restrictions?

answer_card.title: WinRM limitations and workarounds
answer_card.answer_md:
Limitations: no credential delegation for most auth types (network resource errors), many Windows Update API calls blocked, some installers fail, sessions are non-interactive, and no DPAPI access (affects e.g. SQL Server installers).

Workarounds:
- Use **`credssp`** or **`kerberos`** with delegation enabled.
- Use **`become`**: runs as if local, also lifting non-interactive, WUA and DPAPI restrictions.
- Use a **scheduled task** (`win_scheduled_task`): bypasses all restrictions but runs only commands, not modules.
